note: Shown in the report ONLY to a student who declared a difficulty on the assessment page, and ONLY once verified_by_owner is true and checked_on is set (owner gate, Round 10). Every line names its official source; check each against that source before switching this on. Re-check yearly: rules change.

rows.title: Reserved seats in higher education
rows.text: Government colleges and universities, and those receiving government aid, must reserve at least 5% of seats for students with a benchmark disability (40% or more of a specified disability, certified).
rows.source: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 — Section 32

rows.title: Reserved posts in government jobs
rows.text: At least 4% of vacancies in government establishments are reserved for persons with benchmark disabilities.
rows.source: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 — Section 34

rows.title: A scribe and extra time in written exams
rows.text: In written exams, candidates with a benchmark disability can ask for a scribe and compensatory time — at least 20 minutes for every hour of the exam. National entrance exams (JEE, NEET, CUET) follow these guidelines; apply for it when you register for the exam.
rows.source: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities — Guidelines for conducting written examinations for persons with benchmark disabilities (2018)

rows.title: Get your disability certificate (UDID card) early
rows.text: Every reservation and exam facility above asks for a disability certificate. The Unique Disability ID (UDID) card is applied for online; start early, because assessment by a medical board takes time.
rows.source: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment — Unique Disability ID
